text.p: Lehman Brothers raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings per share (EPS) estimates for Israel's Orbotech Ltd, saying the company had a "blowout first quarter".
Lehman, in a report released on Tuesday, raised its EPS estimate for 1997 to $1.99 from $1.81 and its 1998 EPS estimate to $2.35 from $2.13.
Orbotech is a maker of automated optical inspection (AOI) systems for printed circuit boards (PCBs).
"Orbotech reported a 32 percent increase in first quarter EPS to $0.49, well above our expectations," said the report by Lehman's Ted Kundtz.
It said the Orbotech share price had climbed more than 30 percent since the end of March but remained "attractively valued".
"We believe there is a further upside to our new EPS targets and reiterate our 1-Buy rating and raise the one-year price target to $28-$32," the report said.
The shares on Nasdaq are trading at $23-5/8.
Lehman said it was basing its EPS estimates on 17 percent growth in sales in 1997 to $172.7 million and a 19 percent increase in 1998 to $205.8 million.
